body:
WHAT
GraphQuery answers structural questions from the workspace import graph (which file imports which). Five modes: slice (ranked minimal set of files for a topic within a token budget, via personalized PageRank), blast (everything that transitively imports the given files, grouped by hop distance), deps (forward dependency closure with external packages listed separately), structure (top files by PageRank, articulation points, bridges, counts) and rank (most central files, optionally personalized to seeds). Output is capped at 200 lines.

WHY
Without it the agent must open files one by one to learn what depends on what, and cannot judge the blast radius of a change before editing.

WHERE
engine/tools/src/graphQuery.ts — graphQueryTool (op enum, cap() at MAX_LINES 200, one branch per op, error text for missing seeds). Graph logic in engine/core/src/knowledge/graph.ts — loadOrBuildGraph(), buildGraph(), normalizeToId(), pagerank(), blastRadius(), dependencies(), articulationPoints(), slice(), graphStats(); seeds in engine/core/src/knowledge/seeds.ts — resolveSeeds() (paths plus symbol matches).

TEST CHECKLIST
1. Build a temp workspace with a.ts importing b.ts, b.ts importing c.ts, and d.ts importing a.ts; run { op:'blast', files:['c.ts'] } and assert b.ts at distance 1, a.ts at distance 2 and d.ts at distance 3, header 'change amplification: 3 modules'.
2. Run { op:'deps', files:['a.ts'] } on the same workspace; assert b.ts (d1) and c.ts (d2) are listed and, if a.ts also imports 'zod', that 'external: zod' appears.
3. Run { op:'structure' }; assert the header 'graph skeleton of 4 files', a 'top files (pagerank):' section, 'articulation points', 'bridges' and the 'components: ... files: 4 edges: 3' line.
4. Run { op:'rank' } and { op:'slice', query:'a', budget_tokens: 100000 }; assert rank lists files sorted by descending score and slice lists a.ts first with an 'edges among selected:' section containing 'a.ts -> b.ts'.
5. Run { op:'blast', files:['missing.ts'] } and { op:'slice' } with no files/query; assert both return isError:true with the 'needs' message, and a graph with 300 files makes the output end with '[truncated —'.
